Terminal Delight · implementation · 5 November 2026

Prepared Pages Open in 0.2 Seconds

You asked for the 2–3 second wait when opening HTML artifacts to disappear without keeping dozens of browser pages in memory. TD now prepares recent artifacts in advance; those prepared pages open in about a fifth of a second.

01 The Wait Is Shorter

The preparation pays off when you press Alt+O. With 50 panes open, 100 prepared opens filled the visible page in 191 ms at the median; 95 of the 100 finished within 264 ms. Every open used a valid prepared render. This meets the approved 250 ms median and 500 ms tail targets.

Preparation makes the first opening eligible for the fast path. The previous cache already made repeats quick. On the formal brief, an uncached open still took 1.73 seconds median externally, against 2.00 seconds before. The 4× cold-opening target was not reached.

02 Prepare Before the Click

TD watches the newest artifact in the focused pane. After a 400 ms pause, one worker prepares it at the size Alt+O will use. Up to nine recently visited panes remain candidates. Opening cancels preparation at the next browser-call boundary.

A stable section anchor preserves your passage after edits; notes keep their identity. Changed or unknown assets trigger a fresh render. Once capture finishes, TD closes the browser page and can release the images when you leave the tab.

03 What Stays in Memory

The cache lives under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/terminal-delight/pages, normally ~/.cache/terminal-delight/pages. Its 256 MiB budget is disk space. Open pages also need native images and the shared browser; their RAM cost varies with the document and allocator history.

In the 50-pane run, native processes used 333 MiB proportional RAM and Chromium used 156 MiB with the reader visible. Those totals include the terminal and shells. Allocator variation prevents a reliable per-document subtraction. Preparation skips work below 1 GiB available RAM and bounds source size, pixels and PNG output; these admission checks cannot guarantee a browser-RAM ceiling.

04 Checked Through the Real Renderer

The same page retained identical height, all 10 note anchors and all 15 links. The first-viewport pixel difference averaged 0.0014 on a 0–255 scale. The native check confirmed note creation, automatic saving, survival across resize and reopening. Automated tests cover notes, cancellation, asset changes, hidden-buffer release and passage continuity.

Validation and reproduction link to raw timings, source and limitations. The implementation targets the next development wave for 0.5.3. Uncached opening remains a tracked performance limitation.

Preparation stays bounded

Chose
Prepare the newest HTML from up to nine recently visited panes, one page at a time, after a 400 ms dwell; keep completed pixels on disk within the existing 256 MiB budget.
Because
The native fifty-pane run met the prepared-open target while hidden views retained no image tiles. No measured benefit yet justifies preparing additional hovered artifacts.

Meanwhile: carrying on as if you concur.
